messages:
Diego: Hi team — finished DEP enrollment but macOS keeps prompting for a major update (security update) and the installer requires admin. MDM shows me as enrolled but my account isn't in the admin group. Any safe way to let me update?
Jordan (IT): Welcome Diego! Two options: we can push a time-limited admin profile (recommended) or do a remote session and we run the update commands without granting admin. Which do you prefer?
Diego: Prefer temp admin so I can run some other installs while it's up. 30 minutes would be perfect.
Liam: +1 for temp admin. Saves back-and-forth.
Jordan (IT): Ok pushing temp-admin-30m now. You'll see a system prompt to accept a configuration. After acceptance run:
```
sudo softwareupdate --install --all --restart
```
Jordan (IT): Also check FileVault before reboot: System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault. We need it ON and escrowed.
MDM-Bot: Device serial C02ZYX7788 enrolled (profile: employee-standard). Admin assignment: none. Temp profile push: temp-admin-30m queued for C02ZYX7788.
Diego: Prompt received, accepted profile. Ran the `softwareupdate` command. Installer finished and the Mac rebooted.
Diego: Update applied, reboot completed. Everything seems fine.
Jordan (IT): Removing the temp-admin profile now.
MDM-Bot: Profile removed: temp-admin-30m for C02ZYX7788 (actioned by Jordan (IT)).
Diego: Confirmed `sudo -l` returns: user diego is not in the sudoers file. FileVault is ON and recovery key escrowed.
Desktop-Bot: Noted: installed updates include macOS Security Update 2026-06. Logged patch event to asset C02ZYX7788.
Jordan (IT): Logged ticket IT-5425 for the temp admin action and update. Closing loop — welcome aboard Diego! Ping if anything else pops up.
Diego: Thanks y'all :tada: — appreciate the quick help.
